newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola, barley, wheat set new contract lows.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola, barley, wheat set new contract lows.

text.p: WCE canola, barley and feed wheat futures ended at new contract lows in most months.

"XCan sold 750 July, that's what broke the market," a trader said. "Looks like the funds are done buying July-Nov, there were commission sell stops, they liquidated July and Nov and Cargill covered Nov shorts," a trader said. July WCE futures crush margin rose to +2.78 Friday from -0.02 Thursday. About 1,100 July-Nov spread from $32.50 to $29, 600 July-Aug at $1, Sep-Nov $1, Aug-Nov $28.50. Volume was 7,985 lots, or 159,700 tonnes, with 300 hedge lots.
Japan bought 1,000-2,000 tonnes of canola, sources said.
July canola ended down $6.50 at the new low of $388.90, November lost $2.90 at $360.70 after setting a new low at $359.10. All canola contracts except August set new lows.
July flax lost $3 to $331.50 on tight stocks and hedges, Midland Walwyn sold November down $0.70 at $310.50 as it set a new low at $310. July-Nov flax $24. Volume was 295 lots.

Alberta Wheat Pool sold July western barley down $0.40 to $127.30 as it hit a new low of $127.10, December lost $1.40 to a new low of $131.10 as commercials bought late, a trader said. AWP sold July-Oct at $3. Volume was 834 lots.
October peas rose US$0.50 at US$178.50. Oct-Feb US$1.50.
Commercials sold July feed wheat down $0.80 to a new low of $152, October fell $1.30 to the new low of $155.10. Volume was 335 lots.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
